value.SUITABILITY_TASK_PROMPT:
Determine whether the document below is a SYSTEMATIC REVIEW or META-ANALYSIS, which makes it suitable for assessment against the PRISMA 2020 reporting checklist.

A document is SUITABLE if it is:
- A systematic review (a systematic search, with stated methods to identify, select and appraise studies)
- A meta-analysis (a statistical synthesis of the results of several studies)
- A systematic review with a meta-analysis
- One of these kinds of systematic review: a scoping review, a network meta-analysis, an umbrella review (a review of reviews), a rapid review or a living review

A document is NOT SUITABLE if it is:
- Primary research (an RCT, a cohort study, a case-control study, ...)
- A narrative review or literature review without systematic methods
- A protocol for a review, with no results yet
- A clinical guideline
- An editorial, commentary, or opinion piece
- A case report or case series

KEY INDICATORS of a systematic review:
- It describes a systematic search (databases, search terms, dates)
- It states criteria for selecting studies
- It assesses the risk of bias or quality of the included studies
- It may include a PRISMA flow diagram or cite PRISMA
- Its title often says "systematic review" or "meta-analysis"

Assess:
1. is_systematic_review: is this a systematic review (any of the kinds above)?
2. is_meta_analysis: does it include a statistical meta-analysis?
3. document_type: the type of document (e.g. "systematic review with meta-analysis", "scoping review", "narrative review", "RCT")
4. variant: "scoping_review", "network_meta_analysis", "umbrella_review", "rapid_review" or "living_review" when it is one of these kinds, otherwise null
5. rationale: a brief explanation (2-3 sentences)
6. confidence: how confident you are in this assessment (0.0-1.0)

Do not take a document for a systematic review just because it reviews literature: look for the methods above. If uncertain, lean towards NOT SUITABLE and say why in the rationale.

Item 6: Information sources
Checklist wording: Specify all databases, registers, websites, organisations, reference lists and other sources searched or consulted to identify studies. Specify the date when each source was last searched or consulted.
Guidance:
reported: every database (with its platform or interface, for example Ovid), register, website, organisation, reference list and other source searched or consulted, each with the date it was last searched or consulted. One date counts for all sources only if the paper plainly applies it to each.
partly_reported: sources named but dates missing for some or all, or other sources mentioned without naming them, for example "grey literature was searched".
not_reported: no sources named.

Item 7: Search strategy
Checklist wording: Present the full search strategies for all databases, registers and websites, including any filters and limits used.
Guidance:
reported: the full search strategy, exactly as run (every term, Boolean operator, field tag, filter and limit), for every database, register and website searched, in the text.
partly_reported: the full strategy for some sources but not all, or only the terms or concepts searched, or a strategy without its filters and limits.
not_reported: only a statement that a search was done, with no terms.
reported_elsewhere: the paper says where the full strategies are, outside its text, for example "full search strategies in Supplementary Appendix 1"; quote the pointer. If some strategies are in the text and the rest are pointed to, judge reported_elsewhere and say which are in the text.

Item 8: Selection process
Checklist wording: Specify the methods used to decide whether a study met the inclusion criteria of the review, including how many reviewers screened each record and each report retrieved, whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
Guidance:
reported: how many reviewers screened each record (titles and abstracts) and each report retrieved (full texts), whether they worked independently, how disagreements were resolved, and the automation tools used, if any. Silence about automation tools is not a gap.
partly_reported: some of this is missing, for example two reviewers named without saying whether they worked independently, or only the title and abstract stage described.
not_reported: no account of how studies were selected.

- "reported_elsewhere": quote the paper's pointer to where the item is reported (a supplement, a protocol, a registry record)

Item 13d: Synthesis methods: synthesis method
Checklist wording: Describe any methods used to synthesize results and provide a rationale for the choice(s). If meta-analysis was performed, describe the model(s), method(s) to identify the presence and extent of statistical heterogeneity, and software package(s) used.
Guidance:
reported: each synthesis method and the reason it was chosen. not_reported: no synthesis method described.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only. A document is SUITABLE if it is:
- A systematic review (a systematic search, with stated methods to identify, select and appraise studies)
- A meta-analysis (a statistical synthesis of the results of several studies)
- A systematic review with a meta-analysis
- One of these kinds of systematic review: a scoping review, a network meta-analysis, an umbrella review (a review of reviews), a rapid review or a living review

A document is NOT SUITABLE if it is:
- Primary research (an RCT, a cohort study, a case-control study, ...)
- A narrative review or literature review without systematic methods
- A protocol for a review, with no results yet
- A clinical guideline
- An editorial, commentary, or opinion piece
- A case report or case series

KEY INDICATORS of a systematic review:
- It describes a systematic search (databases, search terms, dates)
- It states criteria for selecting studies
- It assesses the risk of bias or quality of the included studies
- It may include a PRISMA flow diagram or cite PRISMA
- Its title often says "systematic review" or "meta-analysis"

Assess:
1. is_systematic_review: is this a systematic review (any of the kinds above)?

5. rationale: a brief explanation (2-3 sentences)
6. confidence: how confident you are in this assessment (0.0-1.0)

Do not take a document for a systematic review just because it reviews literature: look for the methods above. If uncertain, lean towards NOT SUITABLE and say why in the rationale.
